Foreword
The journey to becoming a licensed professional teacher is both demanding and
profoundly rewarding. For graduates in Elementary (BEED) and Secondary Education (BSED),
passing the Licensure Examination for Teachers (LET) is the crucial milestone that marks the
transition from aspiring student to qualified educator. A Compilation Based on the New Table
of Specifications for BEED and BSED was thoughtfully crafted to guide and support examinees
through this pivotal challenge.
The LET evaluates not only foundational knowledge, but also the practical competencies
required in modern classrooms. To reflect evolving educational standards, the Professional
Regulation Commission introduced the new Table of Specifications (TOS). This compilation
adheres strictly to that updated framework, serving as an indispensable resource for a
structured, high-yield review.
What sets this volume apart is its direct alignment with the new TOS through
comprehensive practice items. By working through these questions, examinees gain realistic
practice with the exam's format and rigor while systematically identifying key strengths and
areas for growth. This targeted preparation is essential for building confidence and maximizing
test-day performance.
Beyond exam readiness, becoming a licensed teacher represents a lifelong
commitment to shaping minds and strengthening communities. Approach your review with
discipline, persistence, and purpose. May this book serve not only as a comprehensive study
tool, but also as a catalyst for developing the competence, character, and excellence that
define a truly impactful educator.
I commend your dedication to this noble calling and wish you every success on the exam
and in your future career.
Good luck, and keep striving for excellence!

2. C. STONEHENGE
Stonehenge is not considered a man-

wonder. The search results indicate that
while Stonehenge is an ancient
monument and a UNESCO World
Heritage Site, it is not typically included
in the lists of the Seven Wonders of the

Theater is a collaborative art form that
combines words (dialogue), voice
(acting), movement (choreography), and
visual elements (set design, costumes)
to express meaning and tell a story.

An epistle is a composition in prose or
poetry written in the form of a letter to a
particular person or group. It is often
used in literature to address specific
themes or convey messages in a formal
or reflective manner.
5. D. PHOTOSYNTHESIS
Photosynthesis is the process used by
plants to convert sunlight into chemical
energy, producing glucose and oxygen
from carbon dioxide and water.

61. A. HEAT
· Conduction, convection, and radiation
are ways of transferring or transforming
energy through the use of HEAT.
· Conduction is the transfer of heat
through direct contact between
materials. It occurs when heat energy is
passed from one molecule to another in
a solid.
· Convection involves the transfer of
heat through the movement of fluids
(liquids and gases). Warmer, less dense
fluid rises while cooler, denser fluid
sinks, creating a convection current.
· Radiation is the transfer of energy in
the form of electromagnetic waves, such
as infrared radiation. This method does
not require a medium and can occur in a
vacuum (e.g., heat from the Sun
reaching the Earth).
62. B. ALBERT GERARD
· Solution to practical problems:

· Exception: Pursuance of political
agenda: This is not a beneficial effect,
as it can distort scientific findings for
political gain, undermining the objectivity
of science.
63. A. NOLI ME TANGERE

65. B. WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS
The writ of habeas corpus is a legal
remedy that protects individuals from
unlawful detention or imprisonment. It
allows a person to challenge the legality
of their detention and ensures that they
can appear before a court to determine
whether their imprisonment is justified.
This writ safeguards personal liberty and
prevents enforced disappearances by
compelling authorities to provide a valid
reason for holding someone in custody.
66. D. MICROBIAL CULTURE
A microbial culture involves growing
microorganisms (such as bacteria, fungi,
or viruses) in a controlled environment
to identify the specific pathogen causing
an infection. This process is essential for
diagnosis as it allows observation of the
microorganism's characteristics, which
can then be tested for susceptibility to
antibiotics or other treatments.

Albert Gerard, a 16th century mathematician,

67. D. MAGHAYAG NG KATOTOHANAN
Ang lathalain ay isang anyo ng pagsulat na
naglalayong magbigay ng impormasyon,
opinyon, o pagsusuri tungkol sa isang
paksa. Ang pangunahing layunin nito ay
ang maghayag ng katotohanan, na
nagbibigay diin sa pagiging totoo at tapat
na impormasyon. Sa pamamagitan ng
paghahayag ng katotohanan, ang lathalain
ay nagiging kapani-paniwala at
nakatutulong sa mga mambabasa na
maunawaan ang mga isyu o pangyayari sa
paligid nila. Ang iba pang mga pagpipilian
ay hindi pangunahing layunin ng lathalain.
68. C. LINGUIST

because he was conversant in several
European languages, mastering at least 22
languages throughout his life. His
proficiency in languages allowed him to
communicate effectively, engage in
scholarly discussions, and translate works,
demonstrating his exceptional skill and
passion for language.

70. B. NARCISO CLAVERIA
On November 21, 1849, Narciso Claveria,
the Governor-General of the Philippines,
issued a decree requiring Filipinos to adopt
standardized surnames. This was done to
address administrative issues, as many
Filipinos did not have surnames, leading to
confusion in census-taking and tax
collection. Claveria provided a catalog of
Spanish and local surnames, which
Filipinos were required to choose from, thus
formalizing the use of surnames in the
Philippines.
71. A. EDWARD JENNER
Edward Jenner is considered the "father of
immunology" for his pioneering work in
developing the smallpox vaccine. In 1796,
Jenner discovered that inoculating a person
with cowpox could protect them from
smallpox.

74. B. GRAVITATIONAL
Gravitational Potential Energy relates to an
object's height above the ground.
Examples:
· Child on a Slide: At the top, the child
has gravitational potential energy due to
their height.
· Ripe Guava: Before falling, it has
gravitational potential energy because of
its position in the tree.
· Yoyo: When held up, it has gravitational
potential energy that converts to kinetic
energy when released.

79. D. CONVECTION
It is the process of heat transfer through
the movement of fluids (liquids or
gases). Examples:
· Steam Rising: Hot steam rises as it is
less dense than cooler air.
· Rain Falling from Clouds: The
formation of rain involves convection
currents in the atmosphere.
· Hot Weather Warming Bodies of
Water: Warm air heats the water,
causing convection currents within the
water.
80. C. ALLEGORY

allegory to convey socio-political
messages and critiques of Philippine
society under colonial rule. Through

deeper meanings about social injustices
and the struggle for freedom, making

81. A. PHYLUM
In biological classification, the hierarchy
is structured as follows:
· Domain: The highest taxonomic rank
(e.g., Eukarya).
· Kingdom: The next rank below domain
(e.g., Animalia).
· Phylum: The rank below kingdom (e.g.,
Chordata).
· Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species:
Further subdivisions below phylum.
82. D. FERNANDO AMORSOLO

harmony. "Sari manok" is one of his

84. A. FIRING SQUAD
Rizal's manner of execution was by
firing squad. He was executed on
December 30, 1896, in Manila, where a
military firing squad carried out the
sentence after he was found guilty of
rebellion and sedition. Historical
accounts indicate that only one of the
rifles was loaded with a live bullet, while
the others were blanks, a tactic used to
ease the guilt of the executioners who
knew he was innocent.
85. B. BANGLADESH

territorial disputes over the South China
Sea, while Vietnam, Indonesia, and the
Philippines all have claims in the region,
along with other countries like China,
Malaysia, and Brunei.
86. C. TEODORA ALONSO
The greatest influence on Rizal's life
was his mother Teodora Alonso. She
played a crucial role in shaping Rizal's
character, instilling in him values of
education, discipline, and a sense of
justice. Her teachings and support
significantly impacted his development
as a nationalist and reformist.

126. B. CARNIVORES
In a forest ecosystem, if rabbits are
primary consumers feeding on plants, a
fox that preys on rabbits is classified as
a carnivore.
· Primary consumers (herbivores) feed
directly on producers (plants).
· Carnivores feed on other animals and
are secondary or higher-level
consumers.
· The fox feeds on rabbits (primary
consumers), making it a carnivore.
· Detritivores feed on dead organic
matter; omnivores consume both plants
and animals.

159. B. SALT DEHYDRATES THE
CELL
When cells are exposed to high levels of
salt (sodium chloride), they lose water
through osmosis, causing them to
shrink. This dehydration can lead to
various cellular stress responses and
can damage critical cellular
components. High salt concentrations
draw water out of the cells, leading to a
decrease in cell volume and potentially
affecting their function and viability.

from the Americas.

164. A. CELL-TISSUE-ORGAN-

This sequence represents the biological
hierarchy of organization in living
organisms:
Cell: The basic unit of life.
Tissue: A group of similar cells that
perform a specific function.
Organ: A structure made up of different
types of tissues working together.
Organ System: A group of organs that
work together to perform complex
functions.
Organism: A living entity that can
function independently.

177. C. THE SUM OF THE FORCES
ACTING UPON IT IS ZERO
The statement that is true about the
textbook lying on the table is that the
sum of the forces acting upon it is zero.
When an object is at rest on a surface,
such as a textbook lying on a table, the
forces acting upon it are in equilibrium.
This means that the net force or the
vector sum of all the forces acting on the
object is zero.

179. D. 8
The eight phases of the moon are as
follows:
1. New Moon: The moon is between the
Earth and the sun, and its illuminated
side is facing away from Earth.
2. Waxing Crescent: A small sliver of the
moon becomes visible as it starts to
wax.
3. First Quarter: Half of the moon is
illuminated and visible from Earth.
4. Waxing Gibbous: More than half of the
moon is illuminated as it continues to
wax.
5. Full Moon: The entire face of the moon
is illuminated as it is on the opposite
side of the Earth from the sun.
6. Waning Gibbous: The moon starts to
wane, with more than half still
illuminated.
7. Last Quarter: Again, half of the moon is
illuminated, but the opposite side
compared to the first quarter.
8. Waning Crescent: A small sliver of the
moon is visible as it approaches the new
moon phase again.

of gases that contribute to global
warming and climate change.

Coal is a fossil fuel that takes millions of

greenhouse gas emissions.

182. D. THYROID GLAND
The thyroid gland is located in the front
of the neck and has a distinctive bow tie
or butterfly shape. It regulates
metabolism by producing hormones
such as thyroxine (T4) and
triiodothyronine (T3), influencing
metabolic rate, energy production, and
overall growth and development.
183. B. WALRUS
Walruses are large pinniped mammals
known for their distinctive long tusks,
which are elongated canine teeth. They
inhabit Arctic regions and are well-
adapted to cold environments, often
found on ice floes and in shallow waters.
184. D. ETHOLOGY
Ethology is the scientific and objective
study of animal behavior, particularly in
a natural environment. It focuses on
understanding the evolution,
development, and mechanisms behind
various behaviors exhibited by animals.
185. B. DYAD
In sociology and group dynamics, a
dyad refers to a group consisting of two
members or individuals. It is the
smallest possible group size; a single
individual is a monad, and a group of
three members is called a triad.
186. A. MICHELANGELO
Michelangelo created the renowned
statue of David between 1501 and 1504.
It is celebrated for its artistic excellence
and representation of the biblical hero
David. The sculpture exemplifies
Renaissance art ideals, showcasing
Michelangelo's mastery in portraying
human anatomy and emotion. Originally
intended for the Florence Cathedral, it
was later placed in the Piazza della
Signoria, becoming a symbol of
Florence's civic pride.
187. A. CAVITE MUTINY
The Cavite Mutiny occurred in 1872
when Filipino workers at the Cavite
Naval Yard revolted against the Spanish
colonial government. The Spanish
authorities used this uprising as a
pretext to arrest and execute Fathers
Mariano Gómez, José Burgos, and
Jacinto Zamora, accusing them of
involvement in the mutiny.

plant growth. This depletes dissolved
oxygen levels, especially at night,
leading to fish kills.

205. PLANT CELL WILL SWELL
When a plant cell is placed in a
hypotonic solution, the concentration of
solutes outside the cell is lower than
inside. Water enters the cell via
osmosis. Due to the rigid cell wall, plant
cells can withstand this influx of water,
causing the cell to swell and become
turgid--a normal, healthy state.

231. GRAVITATIONAL
Gravitational potential energy is the
energy an object possesses due to its
position in a gravitational field. When an
object is raised to a higher position, it
gains gravitational potential energy. This
energy is stored and can be converted
into other forms of energy, such as
kinetic energy, when the object moves
or falls. The amount of gravitational
potential energy an object has is directly
proportional to its mass and height
above the ground. This type of potential
energy is important in understanding the
behavior of objects in a gravitational
field and is a fundamental concept in
physics.
232. B. MALTHUSIAN
The Malthusian theory, proposed by
Thomas Robert Malthus in his 1798
work "An Essay on the Principle of
Population", posits that while population
grows exponentially, food supply
increases at an arithmetic rate. This
imbalance leads to inevitable shortages,
resulting in crises such as famine,
disease, and war, which serve as
natural checks on population growth.

Marquez Benitez. In 1941, he was an
administration pensionado to the United
States at the University of Illinois,
Columbia University, and Harvard
University.

solids like spheres, cones, and circles.

12)
· 51 is not prime (divisors: 1, 3, 17, 51)
· Since only one non-prime option is
requested, 51 is the answer.

358. C. A FOOD WEB
REPRESENTS INTERCONNECTIONS,
WHILE A FOOD CHAIN IS ISOLATED
A food chain is a linear sequence
showing how energy flows from one
organism to another, representing a
specific path of feeding relationships. In
contrast, a food web is a complex
network of interconnected food chains,
illustrating multiple feeding relationships
and energy pathways among organisms
in an ecosystem. This makes food webs
more representative of natural
ecosystems compared to the isolated
linear food chain.

364. A. SURFACE TENSION
Small insects can walk on water because of
the attraction between water molecules, which
creates a stretchy sheet forming an invisible
"skin" on the water surface called surface
tension. This phenomenon occurs due to
cohesive forces among water molecules,
making the surface behave like a stretched
elastic membrane that resists external force,
allowing small objects and insects to stay on
the water surface without sinking "surface
tension".

promotes positive mental health benefits such
as increased happiness and decreased
negative emotions.

372. D. P14,880.00
The amount due after adding 8% annual
interest for 3 years on a principal of P12,000
can be calculated using the simple interest
formula for this case since compound interest
frequency is not specified.
Simple interest (SI) = Principal (P) × Rate (r) ×
Time (t)
SI = 12,000 × 0.08 × 3 = 2,880
Total amount due = Principal + Interest =
12,000 + 2,880 = 14,880

376. A. SPRINKLE
Most natural calamities in June and July,
particularly in tropical and monsoon regions,
are often related to heavy rains and floods
caused by prolonged showers, sprinkles, and
thunderstorms. Flash floods commonly occur
as a result of these rains during the rainy
season, which typically peaks in these months.
Therefore, the weather phenomenon that often
occurs in June and July leading to such
conditions is best described as sprinkle or rain
showers.
377. C. IT BECOMES EVIL ACT
When a good action is performed on account of
an evil motive, the moral evaluation of the act
changes, and the action becomes an evil act.
The moral worth of an action depends not only
on the external act but also on the intention or
motive behind it. A good act done for an evil
purpose loses its goodness and becomes
morally wrong because the motive taints the
entire action. Ethical principles affirm that a
good action performed on account of an evil
motive is considered to be an evil act.
378. B. MICROPROCESSOR
Another term for CPU (Central Processing
Unit) is microprocessor. The microprocessor is
essentially the central processing unit
integrated into a single chip. It performs the
core operations of a computer, including
fetching, decoding, and executing instructions,
managing arithmetic and logic operations, and
controlling input/output. While CPUs and
microprocessors are sometimes differentiated
by specific use cases or configurations, in
common terms, the CPU is also called a
microprocessor.

380. A. PROPAGANDA
The reform and national consciousness
campaign in the late 19th century by a group of

López Jaena. The movement aimed to promote
Filipino identity and seek equality and

In the principle of checks and balances, the
legislative branch can check the judiciary by
impeaching judicial officers, including the Chief
Justice. This process holds judicial officials
accountable for misconduct and maintains the
balance of power among branches of
government. The legislature's power to
impeach is a key check on the judiciary,
preventing abuse of power and ensuring
judicial independence is exercised responsibly.

394. C. ENTROPY
Ice melting, salt or sugar dissolving,
making popcorn, and boiling water for
tea are examples of entropy. Entropy is
a scientific concept that measures the
level of disorder or randomness in a
system. In these processes, the system
moves toward a state of higher
disorder -- for example, ice melting
increases molecular movement and
disorder, and sugar dissolving
disperses sugar molecules uniformly in
water.

413. D. HE GOT THE DISEASE
FROM HIS MOTHER.
Hemophilia is an X-linked recessive
BASED ON NEW TABLE OF SPECIFICATIONS (TOS)
EXTENSIVE REVIEWER PROFESSIONAL & GENERAL EDUCATION COMPILED AND RATIONALIZED BY: SIR JAY
disorder, meaning the gene responsible
for the disease is located on the X
chromosome. Since males have only
one X chromosome (inherited from
their mother), a man with hemophilia
must have inherited the defective gene
from his mother. Fathers cannot pass
hemophilia to their sons because they
provide the Y chromosome to male
offspring. Thus, a hemophiliac man got
the disease from his mother.

420. C. RANGE
The range is the statistical measure
that represents the difference between
the highest and lowest values in a data
set. For the data set 60, 70, 75, 80, 85,
95, 100, the range would be 100 -
60 = 40. While the mean, median, and
mode provide measures of central
tendency, the range specifically
captures the spread from highest to
lowest values.

forecasts and advisories, and other
specialized meteorological information
to protect life and property.
451. B. PAHING PANLIBANGAN
Ang pahinang panlibangan ay bahagi
ng pahayagan kung saan makikita ang
mga nakakainjoy na komiks, palaisipan
tulad ng crossword puzzles, at iba
pang mga nakakaaliw na gawain. Ito

452. B. TONY AWARD
The Tony Award, formally known as the
Antoinette Perry Award for Excellence
in Broadway Theatre, is considered
one of the highest honors in the
American theater. It is presented
annually to recognize excellence in live
Broadway productions and
performances. The awards are given
by the American Theatre Wing and The
Broadway League and are regarded as
the theater industry's equivalent to the
Emmy Awards for television and the
Oscars for film.
453. A. CONVICTION
Ang ina ni Jose Rizal na si Doña
Teodora Alonso ay mas pinili pang
makulong at maglakad ng limampung
kilometro bilang parusa sa isang
pekeng kaso kaysa humingi ng tawad o
tanggapin ang paratang. Ipinapakita
nito na siya ay isang babae na may
matibay na paninindigan o conviction,
na hindi sumusuko sa maling paratang
at pinipiling ipagtanggol ang kanyang
dangal at prinsipyo kahit na ito ay
nagdulot ng hirap sa kanya.
454. D. TERESA MAGBANUA
Si Teresa Magbanua ang unang
babaeng mandirigma sa Panay sa
panahon ng Rebolusyong Pilipino. Siya
ay kilala bilang "Joan of Arc ng
Visayas" dahil sa kanyang tapang at
mga naging tagumpay sa mga laban
laban sa mga Kastila. Isa siyang guro
na sumali sa kilusan at pinamunuan
ang mga mandirigmang Pilipino sa iba't
ibang labanan sa Panay.
455. B. PARIS AND HELEN
The tragic lovers in Shakespearean
tragedies include Hamlet and Ophelia,
Anthony and Cleopatra, and Romeo
and Juliet. Paris and Helen, however,
are figures from Greek mythology and
the Trojan War, not characters created
by Shakespeare. Therefore, Paris and
Helen are not tragic lovers in
Shakespeare's works, making this the
correct exception.

50,000

457. D. PORTRAIT OF THE ARTIST
AS FILIPINO
The celebrated play set during the

in pre-World War II Intramuros, Manila,
and explores the life of the Marasigan

458. D. MALTHUSIAN PRINCIPLE
The Malthusian principle, proposed by
Thomas Robert Malthus, states that
population increases geometrically
(exponentially), while food supplies
increase arithmetically (linearly). This
means population grows at a faster
rate than food production, leading to a
potential shortage of resources unless
kept in balance through natural or
preventive checks. This theory
highlights the strain on resources
caused by rapid population growth.
459. D. PLANTS
Decomposers are organisms that break
down dead organic material, recycling
nutrients back to the ecosystem.
Earthworms, termites, and fungi are all
considered decomposers because they
consume dead matter and help
decompose it. However, plants are
producers, not decomposers, as they
create their own food through
photosynthesis rather than breaking
down organic material.
460. D. PANGASINAN
The Sayaw sa Bangko, or the Bench
Dance, originated in Pangasinan,
Philippines. This traditional folk dance
is performed by couples balancing on a
narrow bench and showcases skill,
balance, and coordination. It is deeply
rooted in the cultural heritage of
Pangasinan and often performed
during town fiestas as a symbol of the
region's rich traditions.
461. C. CEDULAS
Bonifacio and the Katipuneros tore
their cedulas (tax certificates) on
August 26, 1896, signaling open
rebellion against Spain. This act,
known as the "Cry of Balintawak,"
symbolized their rejection of Spanish
colonial rule and was a formal
declaration of separation from Spain.
462. C. TINIKLING.
This traditional Philippine bamboo-
dance has gained wide international
exposure, including strong presence in
the United States, through schools,
cultural programs, and performances
by Filipino communities abroad.
463. D. TERRITORIAL WAR
The dispute over the Spratly Islands in
the South China Sea primarily involves
issues related to territorial sovereignty
and control. Multiple countries including
China, the Philippines, Vietnam,
Malaysia, Taiwan, and Brunei claim
ownership of the islands due to their
strategic location, rich natural
resources, and control of vital sea
lanes. This has led to heightened
tensions and confrontations that are
best characterized as a territorial war
rather than mere land grabbing or
illegal migration.
464. A. LEANING TOWER OF PISA
The Leaning Tower of Pisa in Italy is
famous for its unintentional tilt caused
by unstable and soft subsoil beneath its
shallow foundations. Construction
began in 1173, and the tower started
leaning as early as 1178 during the
building of the third floor due to the
uneven settling of the ground. Despite
several attempts to correct the tilt by
adjusting the construction of upper
floors, it continued to lean, becoming
an iconic architectural landmark known
worldwide for this unique
characteristic.
465. A. UGNAYAN
Ang pinakamahalagang gamit ng wika
ay ang pagbibigay-diin sa pagkaka-isa
ng mga mamamayan sa pamamagitan
ng ugnayan.
Ang wika ay nagsisilbing pangunahing
instrumento upang magkaisa ang isang
lipunan, magtulungan, at magbuklod sa
kabila ng pagkakaiba-iba sa kultura,
tradisyon, at diyalekto.
466. A. CONVECTION
Hot air rising above a fire, ice melting,
and rain falling from clouds are
examples of convection. Convection is
the process by which heat is
transferred through the movement of
fluids such as liquids and gases. When
a part of a fluid is heated, it becomes
less dense and rises, while cooler,
denser fluid sinks, creating convection
currents. This natural circulation
transfers heat and causes various
phenomena in the environment.
467. B. B.F. SKINNER
Naturalism in early childhood
development is to Jean Jacques
Rousseau as behavior modification is
to B.F. Skinner. Rousseau emphasized
the natural development of the child in
education, advocating for learning in
harmony with nature. Skinner, on the

behaviorism, particularly behavior
modification through operant

469. C. AFFECTIVE
When individuals base their moral
judgments on how their actions will
affect others and the broader
community, they are likely in the
affective stage (Stage 3: Interpersonal
Relationships) of values development.
This stage, part of Kohlberg's
Conventional Level, emphasizes living
up to social expectations, valuing
relationships, and considering how
choices impact others and societal
norms.
470. A. POVERTY LINE
The poverty line is the level of personal
or family income below which one is
classified as poor according to
governmental standards. It represents
the minimum income deemed
adequate to meet basic needs such as
food, shelter, and clothing.
Governments calculate it based on the
cost of living and essential expenses,
and it is used to identify those living in
poverty for social and economic policy
purposes.
471. C. PRESERVATION OF
FILIPINO ART
The main contribution of a GAMABA
(Gawad sa Manlilikha ng Bayan) artist
to society is the preservation of Filipino
art. GAMABA artists are recognized by
the Philippine government for their
exceptional skills in traditional folk arts,
serving as custodians of cultural
heritage.
472. A. EDWARD JENNER
Vaccination against cholera, anthrax,
and rabies are attributed to Louis
Pasteur, while vaccination against
smallpox is credited to Edward Jenner.
Jenner pioneered the smallpox vaccine
in 1796 by using material from cowpox
lesions to confer immunity against
smallpox, a breakthrough that laid the
foundation for modern immunology and
vaccination practices.
473. B. BIOLUMINESCENCE
Light produced by a chemical reaction
within a living organism is called
bioluminescence. It occurs when
chemical energy is converted into light
energy through a reaction involving
substances like luciferin and the
enzyme luciferase. This natural glowing
phenomenon is common in organisms
such as fireflies, certain marine
animals, fungi, and bacteria.
474. C. JOHANN STRAUSS II
The Blue Danube, the most famous
waltz ever written, epitomizes the
symphonic richness and variety of
dance music. This waltz was composed
by the Austrian composer Johann
Strauss II in 1866. It has become one
of the most consistently popular pieces
in classical music and is considered an
iconic work of the Viennese waltz
tradition.
475. B. PLANTS
All these are examples of abiotic
factors in the ecosystem except plants.
Abiotic factors are the non-living
components such as light, minerals,
and water that influence the
environment. Plants are living
organisms and are considered biotic
factors because they interact with and
depend on abiotic factors within an
ecosystem.
476. A. DIDACTIC
There are literature types that aim to
inspire and develop values; these types
belong to didactic literature. Didactic
literature is specifically designed to
teach moral lessons or impart values to
readers while often entertaining them.
It uses stories, fables, parables, and
other forms to instruct and improve the
moral character of its audience.
477. B. PROCEDURAL
Knowledge related to methods or
operations which is goal-oriented, with
the goal being the actual performance
of a task that requires skills, is known
as procedural knowledge. This type of
knowledge involves knowing how to do
something, focusing on the steps or
actions required to complete tasks. It is
practical, action-oriented, and typically
acquired through practice and
experience.

479. B. SECONDARY ECOLOGICAL
SUCCESSION
The phenomenon described is called
secondary ecological succession. It
occurs when an ecosystem recovers
after a disturbance, such as wildfires,
that destroys existing vegetation but
leaves the soil intact and viable. Over
time, plants like trees and bushes
gradually recolonize the area, leading
to a reestablishment of the ecosystem.
480. D. LOOSE
The correct word is "loose," which is an
adjective meaning not tight or not firmly
attached. In the sentence, "Her figure
was carelessly wrapped in a loose
gown, trimmed with fur; but its grace
indicated its symmetry," "loose"
describes the gown as being not tightly
fitted around her figure. The other
options do not fit grammatically or
contextually: "loss" (noun), "lose"
(verb), and "lost" (past tense
verb/adjective).
481. C. 16 AND 18
The two consecutive even integers
whose sum is 34 are 16 and 18.
Setting the first integer as , the next
consecutive even integer is  + 2. The
equation is:
 + ( + 2) = 34
Simplifying,
2 + 2 = 34   2 = 32    = 16
Here is a shorter step-by-step
computation:
1. Let x = first even integer
2. Then x+2 = second even integer
3. Equation: x+(x+2)=34
4. Simplify: 2x+2=34
5. Solve: 2x=32  x=16
Answer: 16 and 18
482. D. TARANTELLA
The Tarantella is a folk dance in Italy
characterized by light, quick steps and
teasing, flirtatious behavior between
partners. Women dancers frequently
carry tambourines while performing this
lively dance. It is one of the most
recognized traditional southern Italian
dances.
483. A. PSEUDONYM
Filipino heroes, to avoid identity and
persecution during the Spanish Era, did
not use their true names in propaganda
writings but instead used pseudonyms.
A pseudonym is a fictitious name used
to conceal their real identity while
expressing their nationalist ideas
safely.
484. A. ALA PATRIA
The poem "Ala Patria" by Jose Rizal
tells us how beautiful the Philippines is
and expresses his desire for Filipinos
to learn from their past and see the
truth about how the world views the
country. It reflects Rizal's deep love for
his homeland and his call for
awareness and awakening among
Filipinos.
485. B. GLOBAL WARMING
The gravest threat to mankind in the
21st century is global warming. It is
causing climate change with severe
consequences such as extreme
weather events, rising sea levels, and
biodiversity loss. This threat is widely
recognized as a critical global issue
requiring urgent action.
486. C. DYNAMITE FISHING
Knowing how important marine
ecosystems are, the government
strictly regulates dynamite fishing. This
illegal and destructive method causes
severe damage to marine habitats and
biodiversity, thus its regulation is critical
for marine conservation.

488. B. ALBERT GIRARD
Albert Girard is credited with publishing
a treatise on trigonometry containing
the earliest use of the abbreviations
sin, tan, and sec for sine, tangent, and
secant, respectively, in 1626. This
notation became the foundation for
modern trigonometric symbols.

490. B. METAPHYSICAL
Metaphysical personhood is based on
the ability to distinguish between the
visible, sensed, and invisible world and
includes reasoning and thinking. It
involves innate capacities such as self-
awareness, imagination, thought, and
reason, distinguishing it from other
types of personhood like moral,
physical, or legal.
491. D. MUTUALISM
Bees gathering nectar from flowers,
which they use to make food,
demonstrate mutualism. This
relationship benefits both: bees get
food, while flowers get pollinated,
aiding their reproduction.
492. D. LITERATURE
Prose and poetry are two general types
of the art known as literature. Literature
encompasses written works that
express ideas, stories, emotions, or
information through language, with
prose being ordinary written or spoken
language, and poetry characterized by
rhythmic and often metaphorical
language.
493. D. MARIE CURIE
Marie Curie is credited with the
discovery of polonium and radium in
1898, which led to the use of
radioactive materials in the field of
medicine. She and her husband Pierre
Curie conducted the research that
isolated these elements and advanced
the understanding of radioactivity.
494. D. KABAYAO
Gilopez Kabayao is a violist known for
bringing classical violin music to the
masses in the Philippines. He had a
long concert career and contributed
significantly to popularizing classical
music among Filipinos.
495. C. UNSUNG HEROES
Overseas Filipino workers boost the
Philippine economy through their
remittances, while sacrificing
separation from their families. Because
of their vital yet often underrecognized
contributions and sacrifices, they are
called unsung heroes.
496. B. EPISTLE
Epistles are a form of literature whose
purpose is to educate or inform. They
are formal letters or written
communications often used to convey
knowledge, advice, or information to
specific audiences, fitting the category
of educational or informative literature.

499. C. KINETIC
Potential energy is the stored energy
(like that in a battery), while kinetic
energy is the energy of motion, which
applies to a moving electric fan. The
fan's blades in motion represent kinetic
energy.
500. B. PRESIDENTIAL
The form of government characterized
by the separation of powers, dividing
authority among the executive,
legislative, and judicial branches, is the
presidential system. This system
ensures that each branch operates
independently with checks and
balances on each other.
501. C. RECIPROCAL
The relationship between science and
technology, providing modern products
and processes to society, is described
as reciprocal. This means they
influence and benefit each other and
society in a mutual, interactive way.
502. C. LOPEZ JAENA, M. H. DEL

PROFESSIONAL EDUCATION HIGH-YIELD
LET BULLETS 500+
This high-yield bullets, covers essential legislation, including RA 10912 (Continuing Professional Development Act),
which requires teachers to earn 15 CPD units for license renewal, and RA 7836 (Philippine Teachers Professionalization
Act of 1994), enacted under the 1987 Constitution to govern teacher licensure. Teacher licenses may be revoked for
neglecting CPD requirements, an exclusive power held by the Board for Professional Teachers.
Professional ethics define integrity as moral courage, while spirituality encompasses love, service, and freedom. A
21st-century teacher is characterized as a lifelong learner and a facilitator of learning rather than a traditional lecturer.
Professionalism requires upholding fairness, gender sensitivity, and empathy toward learners while avoiding harmful
rumors.
National and regional standards are key components of the review: the Philippine Professional Standards for
Teachers (PPST) aligns with career stage qualification levels, while the ASEAN Qualifications Reference Framework
(AQRF) establishes eight standardized qualification levels across the region. Ultimately, success in teaching is measured
by the learners' acquired competencies. Teachers are expected to monitor their behavior to align words with actions, serve
as role models, and collaborate harmoniously with community and local government officials.
Curriculum foundations span philosophical, sociological, and psychological principles, emphasizing both learner and
societal needs. Curriculum development is a continuous process supported by all stakeholders with the child at the center.
Models such as Hilda Taba's stress diagnosing learner needs at the beginning, while a spiral curriculum systematically
revisits topics with increasing complexity. Furthermore, RA 10533 (Enhanced Basic Education Act) mandates the use of the
mother tongue as the medium of instruction in early grades.
Effective pedagogy involves aligning learning outcomes with lesson content, integrating technology through blended
and online learning, and applying culturally responsive teaching that values diversity. Classroom management focuses on
fostering safety, respect, and active engagement. Grounded in learning theories--such as behaviorism, cognitivism,
constructivism, and social learning--instruction promotes critical thinking, reflection, and creativity.
Assessment strategies range from formative and summative evaluations to authentic assessments. Additionally,
action research enables teachers to identify and solve classroom issues collaboratively, advancing professional growth and
refining instruction.

EXTENSIVE REVIEWER PROFESSIONAL & GENERAL EDUCATION COMPILED AND RATIONALIZED BY: SIR JAY
GENERAL EDUCATION HIGH-YIELD
LET BULLETS 500+
This is the bulleted and simplified review compilation based on the new TOS, designed to help aspiring
teachers prepare effectively for the Licensure Examination for Teachers (LET). The questions span critical areas
such as language and communication skills, literature, social sciences, Philippine history, educational psychology,
teaching principles, classroom management, and basic sciences.
Language and Filipino communication questions cover grammatical elements like gitling (hyphen), kuwit
(comma), ellipses, types of panlapi (affixes), syntax, ponolohiya (phonology), and literary devices such as
metaphors and fables. These test examinees' grasp of Filipino language mechanics and literary forms needed for
effective communication and instruction.
Social science and history questions cover key events like the Galleon Trade, Philippine revolutions, and
contributions of national heroes such as Rizal and Bonifacio. Governance topics include knowledge of the Bill of
Rights, political participation, and legal frameworks such as the Local Government Code and constitutional writs
like Habeas Corpus and Amparo. Understanding cultural sensitivity and Filipino identity is also evaluated.
Science questions focus on fundamental concepts in biology, physics, chemistry, and environmental
science. Candidates are assessed on scientific methods, ecosystems (producers, consumers, decomposers),
energy sources, states of matter, reproduction, and environmental conservation issues--including the causes of
climate change, renewable energy, and pollution control. These ensure teachers can integrate scientific literacy
into their classrooms.
Professional education items assess teaching methodologies, assessment types (formative and
summative), learner characteristics, differentiated instruction, ethics, and professional responsibilities. Real-life
teaching scenarios test candidates' problem-solving and classroom management skills.
Sample math questions test computational and reasoning skills relevant to daily teaching, including finding
the LCM and GCD, solving equations, and basic geometry.
This compilation strictly aligns with the structure and competencies mandated by the new TOS--utilizing a
multiple-choice format with one best answer--providing a comprehensive review to boost confidence and
competence.

MOCK BOARDS - PROFESSIONAL
EDUCATION 3500+ QUESTIONS
The "Mock Board - Professional Education 3500+ Questions" is a comprehensive review resource designed
to help aspiring licensure examinees prepare effectively for the Professional Education subject. It offers thousands
of practice questions covering a wide range of key topics such as teaching professions, principles of teaching,
educational technology, child and adolescent development, foundations of education, and assessment of learning.
This extensive question bank simulates board exam conditions, allowing examinees to practice answering
thousands of questions, manage time, and familiarize themselves with exam formats.
The questions include multiple-choice formats that test knowledge on education theories, classroom
management, curriculum design, learning assessment, and educational laws and codes. Examinees can expect
to encounter items on cognitive development, instructional strategies, educational psychology, and various
teaching methodologies. The mock board exams typically come with answer keys for immediate feedback and
self-assessment, enabling efficient review and mastery of content.
This tool is ideal for serious LET (Licensure Exam for Teachers) candidates looking for a thorough drill
experience across all subtopics in Professional Education. It encourages active practice and repetition of
questions to build confidence and improve retention before the actual board exam. Many versions also provide
instruction on proper test-taking strategies and handling exam pressure, enhancing readiness for the Professional
Education portion of the teacher licensure exam.
Overall, the Mock Board - Professional Education 3500+ Questions offers a detailed, exam-oriented review
platform for those preparing for their teaching licensure, with a strong focus on professional knowledge and applied
pedagogy in education.
